## Trip highlights

### Buenos Aires

The first city on the itinerary combines European architecture, expansive green spaces and neighborhoods with distinct characters.

On a sightseeing tour, you'll see central squares and monuments, stroll through La Boca and San Telmo, and visit Plaza Dorrego and Plaza de Mayo. Your guide will tell you about the Casa Rosada and Evita Perón.

On the evening of day two, enjoy a tango show at Tango Porteño with dinner and drinks.

### A gaucho ranch

A full day is devoted to the traditions of the Argentine Pampas.

At Estancia Santa Susana, you'll learn about gaucho life, see folk dancing and tango, and watch riders demonstrate their lasso and horsemanship skills.

The visit ends with a chance to sample Argentine meat.

### Mendoza and the Uco Valley

Mendoza lies in an arid region, but an extensive network of irrigation channels and tens of thousands of planted trees keep the city green.

After exploring the city, spend the next day visiting wineries in the Uco Valley at the foot of the Andes. With a specialist guide, you'll visit three wineries, learn how grapes are grown and harvested and how wine is made, and take part in a tasting.

Malbec is the main grape variety featured on the tour. Lunch is served at one of the wineries.

### Santiago

The tour of the Chilean capital starts at San Cristóbal Hill and Metropolitan Park before continuing to the historic center.

You'll see the Governor's House, the Central Post Office, La Moneda Palace, Plaza de Armas and the Metropolitan Cathedral. The tour ends in Santiago's modern districts, home to hotels, restaurants, bars and shopping centers.

### Viña del Mar and Valparaíso

Spend a full day on the Chilean coast.

Known as the Garden City, Viña del Mar has leafy streets and nearby Pacific beaches. Its Fonck Museum has exhibits on Chilean archaeology and history, including jewelry and ceramics made by Indigenous peoples.

Valparaíso is built on hills, with funiculars and stairways connecting different levels of the city. Cerro Concepción overlooks the port and the coast.

### Concha y Toro

On the last full day of the trip, visit the Concha y Toro vineyards.

The company was founded in 1883. On the tour, you'll walk through the vineyards and the European-style park, see the winery building and taste several wines.

Lunch is available on site at an additional cost.
